purpose: Record the preferred machine-readable and critical-edition baselines for the first Flood calibration before feature extraction.

baselines.preferred_critical_baseline: Nathan Wasserman, The Flood: The Akkadian Sources: A New Edition, Commentary, and a Literary Discussion, OBO 290, 2020
baselines.reason: Peer-reviewed synoptic edition collecting the Akkadian flood sources from Old Babylonian through Neo-Assyrian/Neo-Babylonian, including Gilgamesh XI, with philological commentary and glossary.
baselines.access_note: Publisher identifies the book as open access.
baselines.topa_use: Use source-by-source witnesses; do not flatten the Akkadian flood corpus into one composite witness.

baselines.preferred_critical_baseline: Andrew R. George, The Babylonian Gilgamesh Epic: Introduction, Critical Edition and Cuneiform Texts, 2003
baselines.reason: Critical edition collecting known cuneiform sources; SOAS repository identifies it as peer-reviewed and publicly available.
baselines.topa_use: Cross-check Wasserman's Flood-specific synoptic treatment against George's Gilgamesh edition for Tablet XI.

baselines.preferred_machine_baseline: ETCBC BHSA (Biblia Hebraica Stuttgartensia Amstelodamensis) frozen Text-Fabric version
baselines.reason: Machine-readable Hebrew Bible with linguistic annotations and versioned fixed datasets; suited to reproducible extraction and syntax-aware controls.
baselines.license: CC BY-NC 4.0 for the data; attribution required; commercial use restricted.
baselines.topa_use: Freeze one explicit BHSA version before extraction; preserve the received-text reading and run separate source-partition sensitivity rather than modifying the base text.

baselines.reason: Versioned UTF-8 Arabic text with explicit distribution terms and a stable download surface.
baselines.license: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 with verbatim-copy requirement; changing the text is not allowed.
baselines.topa_use: Store verbatim source text if mirrored; normalization/tokenization must be a derived analysis layer, never a replacement of the canonical source file.

baselines.preferred_machine_baseline: GRETIL Satapatha-Brahmana, Madhyamdina recension (input by John Robert Gardner)
baselines.reason: GRETIL explicitly lists a UTF-8 electronic text for the Madhyamdina recension, allowing the exact recension to be frozen rather than using only an English translation.
baselines.topa_use: Freeze the Madhyamdina recension and exact 1.8.1 locus before coding; later Manu/Matsya retellings remain separate descendants unless independence is demonstrated.

anti_bias_rules: A newer edition does not erase older witness history; citations and variant readings remain traceable.
Machine-readable convenience does not outrank critical philology.
Derived normalization layers must be hash-linked to the immutable source text.
No cross-language lexical score is permitted from English/Russian/Ukrainian translations alone.
If two defensible editions materially change a feature, mark the feature EDITION_SENSITIVE rather than choosing the favorable reading.
